follow100Note: Spotify keeps about $21.04 of every $100 — but that includes a $5.74 boost from finance income (mostly a paper gain) and a $1.69 tax benefit, not just operating profit. Rows may not add exactly due to rounding.
footerNote: Spotify reports in euros under IFRS. Dollar figures are converted at €1 = $1.1733 (USD:Euro 0.8523 at Sep 30, 2025, the rate in Spotify's own release). As reported: revenue €4,272M · gross profit €1,351M · operating income €582M · net income €899M.

oneTimers: Operating expenses included (€16)M of 'social charges' — Swedish payroll taxes on share-based pay that swing with Spotify's share price; they were a €16M credit this quarter as the share price fell, versus a €53M cost a year ago, and came in €41M below forecast.

The quarter carried a €72M income tax benefit (versus a €98M tax expense a year ago), including a €202M benefit from the accelerated deduction of previously capitalized US R&D costs under new US tax rules and a €50M benefit tied to the Exchangeable Notes.

Finance income included a €197M paper gain on the Exchangeable Notes — the notes are worth less when Spotify's share price falls, which books as income, and it reverses if the share price rises. Diluted EPS of €3.28 is calculated after removing that gain (on €702M of income, not €899M).
otherDetail: Finance items netted +$287M — a €197M paper gain on the Exchangeable Notes plus €57M of interest earned on Spotify's cash pile, less €17M of finance costs (mostly foreign-exchange losses and lease interest).

segments.name: Premium
segments.note: Subscriptions — 281 million people paying monthly, up 12% YoY; revenue per user (ARPU) €4.53, down 4% on currency moves but flat in constant currency.

segments.name: Ad-Supported
segments.note: The free tier's advertising business — revenue fell 6% as podcast ad pricing softened, though it was flat in constant currency; its gross margin jumped to 18.4%.

takeaways.text: Premium subscribers grew 12% to 281 million and monthly active users passed 700 million for the first time, reaching 713 million. Premium revenue grew 9% to €3,826M, with price rises offsetting a 4% dip in revenue per user caused by currency moves.
takeaways.title: Subscribers keep compounding

takeaways.text: Gross margin rose to 31.6%, up 53 bps YoY, driven by the Ad-Supported segment, whose gross margin jumped to 18.4% on better podcast and music contribution. Premium gross margin slipped to 33.2% as video podcast costs rose.
takeaways.title: Margins widened — mostly in ads

takeaways.text: Free cash flow hit a Q3 record €806M and the cash pile reached €9.1B. But net income of €899M was flattered: €245M of net finance income included a €197M paper gain on the Exchangeable Notes, and the quarter carried a €72M tax benefit including a €202M one-off from US R&D tax rules.
takeaways.title: A record quarter for cash — but profits were flattered

verdict: Spotify grew revenue 7% to €4.3B (about $5.0B) as Premium subscribers hit 281 million, while a tax benefit and a paper gain on its Exchangeable Notes lifted net income to €899M — well above operating income of €582M.
